thread:
Alice Chen: quick RFC follow-up — I want to capture tradeoffs for a long-term refactor: split control plane into a tiny customer-side agent + central controlplane, vs full per-customer controlplane. thinking about networking/perf/ops. :thinking:
Marco Diaz: short version: thin agent reduces customer footprint but pushes complexity to controlplane (connection mgmt, auth, routing).
Priya Patel: agreed. also important: how much trust do we place in the agent? KMS/HSM access, secret lifecycle, certs.
Ben Jacobs: ops POV: peering vs private endpoints. peering keeps traffic direct but needs cross-account routing rules and route table churn. endpoints (privatelink-style) simplify routing but increase egress costs and require ENI mgmt.
Alice Chen: list of constraints I care about: 1) zero-trust boundaries 2) lifecycle of keys 3) telemetry & debug access without opening customer network 4) minimal customer infra changes 5) ability to fallback to hosted when private is degraded
Marco Diaz: for zero-trust, mTLS + short-lived certs (SPIFFE/SPIRE) looks good. agent requests cert from controlplane over mutual TLS bootstrap. controlplane never stores long-term private keys.
Priya Patel: cert rotation story: agent should support automatic rotation and CA rekey without customer network changes. also offline bootstrap for air-gapped installs (signed CSR exchange).
Ben Jacobs: performance: we tested options: long-lived tunnel (TLS over TCP) with HTTP/2 multiplexing has lower P95 than per-request TLS. connection pooling + keepalive critical.
Alice Chen: major network topologies considered:
- Cross-account VPC peering (static routes)
- Transit gateway (central hub)
- Private endpoint per customer (ENI or interface endpoint) with proxy relays
- Agent-initiated outbound TLS tunnel to controlplane (no inbound from us)

Marco Diaz: peering: pros = low-latency, no additional proxies. cons = route explosion for many customers, cross-account IAM work, and egress path complexity.
Priya Patel: transit-gw: easier to scale and centralize routes but expensive and a single billing bucket. also regional limits.
Ben Jacobs: endpoints: nice for least-privilege inbound access. but ENI scaling and IP management is annoying. For AWS privatelink we hit ENI quotas on spike tests.
Alice Chen: my leaning: default = outbound agent-initiated tunnels + optional privatelink for customers that require inbound-only. fallback routes to hosted via policy if tunnel unhealthy.
Marco Diaz: sounds reasonable. need to define interface boundary clearly: what does agent own vs controlplane?
Priya Patel: proposal for boundaries:
- Agent owns: connection stack (tunnels, keepalives), local KV cache, metrics export, minimal auth (CSR + mTLS), local model pinning policy, healthchecks to controlplane.
- Controlplane owns: routing decisions, model artifacts, global audit logs, rollout control, certificates CA, billing/quotas.

Ben Jacobs: operationally, agent must expose local debug port (127.0.0.1) only and a signed trace upload endpoint to controlplane. no open SSH or wide admin surfaces.
Alice Chen: security details: use mTLS with short TTL certs + OIDC-backed bootstrap token for the very first connection. example bootstrap flow:
1) Customer creates bootstrap API key (scoped) in controlplane UI
2) Agent uses API key to request a one-time bootstrap JWT
3) Controlplane issues a short-lived cert for mTLS (5m) after validating CSR
4) Agent rotates certs via CSR renewal, controlplane rotates CA regularly

Marco Diaz: and for air-gapped: exchange signed bundle offline, agent verifies controlplane signature locally. document that as separate flow.
Priya Patel: DNS and service discovery: keep a private regional controlplane fqdn per region (e.g., control-eu.central.redwood.local) and publish via Private Hosted Zone when using privatelink/peering. Agent falls back to public DNS for hosted fallback.

Ben Jacobs: example agent config (pseudo YAML):

```yaml
agent:
  mode: outbound-tunnel
  controlplane_fqdns:
    - cp-eu.central.redwood.internal
  bootstrap_api_key: "redacted"
  cert_ttl: 300s
  keepalive:
    interval: 30s
    timeout: 90s
  local_debug_port: 127.0.0.1:17000
  allowed_subnets: ["10.0.0.0/16"]
```

Alice Chen: routing policy idea: controlplane decides per-tenant whether to route to hosted replicas, dedicated pool, or local cache; agent enforces on-device routing and cache TTL. we must ensure cache poison protection (signed artifacts).

Marco Diaz: metrics/health: agent should push compressed metrics over the same tunnel with labels: tenant_id, region, vpc_id. controlplane can request debug snapshot on demand. add circuit-breaker if RTT > threshold, switch to hosted fallback.

Priya Patel: audit & compliance: all agent actions must be logged locally and uploaded to an append-only audit stream in controlplane; support customer-side audit copying to S3 or SIEM via signed push.

Ben Jacobs: want to call out cost implications: transit-gw and privatelink both add aws costs; tunnel model shifts cost to egress data + our central infra. need to model 3-year TCO for customers.

Alice Chen: open questions I want answers on before RFC v2:
- Do we standardize on tunnel-first with opt-in privatelink, or gate by contract?
- How do we do zero-touch onboarding for large customers (10s of accounts) with minimal route table surgery?
- What SLAs can we provide if customers opt for agent-only (no privatelink)?

Marco Diaz: action items:
- I'll spike connection pooling + h2 perf numbers this week.
- Priya, can you draft cert bootstrap sequences and offline bundle requirements?
- Ben, can you run ENI quota + privatelink cost model on 50 customers?

Priya Patel: noted. drafting offline bundle doc now. publishing to the private architecture drive later today.

Ben Jacobs: starting quota/cost run. adding to infra backlog.
